rationale: Section 6.3 sets the Top-Up Price 'equal to the Dilutive Price' and Schedule II Example 1 shows the Investor paying $55,556 for 55,556 shares; 6.5 makes it an election. The Note to Draft says the Company will argue for a nominal price, which has the sides backwards, so the mode is K (what a customary top-up is), with I secondary. Material: the client's anti-dilution protection costs him the full round price. D1.

what_went_wrong: No clause awarding legal fees to the prevailing party; attorneys' fees appear only inside the general definition of Losses for the breach indemnities

rationale: The task asked for customary boilerplate; the expert's agreement and Opus's both have the clause.
